Assertion (A): Nanga Parbat and Namcha Barwa are considered the two syntaxial bends or 'anchors' of the Himalayan arc.

Reason (R): Nanga Parbat marks the western end where the Indus river takes a sharp gorge-cutting turn, while Namcha Barwa marks the eastern end where the Brahmaputra (Tsangpo) makes its Great Bend before entering India.

Select the correct answer from the code given below:

_aimcq_options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Himalayan Syntaxes: The Himalayan mountain arc is anchored at both ends by dramatic river gorges cut by antecedent rivers.

Statement Analysis
  • Assertion (A) is correct: Geographers describe Nanga Parbat (west) and Namcha Barwa (east) as the two syntaxial bends of the Himalaya.
  • Reason (R) is correct and explains (A): At Nanga Parbat (Pakistan-administered), the Indus cuts a deep gorge as it turns south; at Namcha Barwa (Tibet-Arunachal Pradesh border), the Yarlung Tsangpo/Brahmaputra makes its famous 'Great Bend' (Dihang Gorge) before entering India as the Siang.
  • This antecedent drainage evidence is key proof that these rivers are older than the Himalayan uplift itself.
Know More: Himalayan Syntaxes
  • Western syntaxis — Nanga Parbat (8,126 m), Pakistan-administered territory, where the Indus makes its dramatic southward gorge.
  • Eastern syntaxis — Namcha Barwa (7,782 m), Tibet-Arunachal border, where the Yarlung Tsangpo/Brahmaputra bends sharply south (the 'Great Bend') to enter India as the Siang.
  • Both syntaxes are zones of extremely rapid tectonic uplift and erosion, among the most active on Earth.
